bar.name: Onshape Sketch toolbar
bar.note: A separate bar from the feature toolbar. It appears only while a sketch is open.

ships.where: sketch-solve.ts constraint 'length' -- distance only, no angle

SketchFeature.shape 'circle' -- two points read as a diameter (lib/sketch-arc.ts circleOf()) -- plus the toolbar's Circle button (ModelEditor.tsx startCircleSketch()). Not a centre-plus-drag click: that needs the click-to-draw surface chrome2d names below, which still does not exist
lib/sketch-arc.ts filletCorner() -- trims both adjacent edges and inserts an arc via a bulge (tan(includedAngle/4)) -- wired to a per-corner radius field in the Rules panel (SketchConstraints.tsx).
ships.partial: corner-bearing sketches only, and reachable only from the Rules panel -- there is no click-a-corner-on-the-canvas surface, because there is no 2D canvas. A circle sketch renders no Rules panel and has no corners, so Round is unreachable for it by design. The refusal message that explains this has been wrong three times in a row, each generation naming a remedy the student could not reach; it now names none and just states what is true. This entry is an artefact under test like any other -- it overclaimed twice before saying this much.

build.name: the representation
build.why: DECIDED (build 1, panel-reviewed): SketchFeature gained two optional fields, additive to the existing points: Array<[number,number]> -- shape?: 'circle' (a tag, not an inference, read by circleOf()) and bulges?: Record<edge, number> (tan(includedAngle/4) on the edge leaving a corner, read by arcFromBulge()/tessellate() in lib/sketch-arc.ts). A sketch saved before this field existed has neither key and still loads, builds and renders exactly as before -- see scripts/check-sketch-compat.mjs. lib/sketch-solve.ts (the constraint relaxation solver) is UNCHANGED; both write-back paths already spread {...f, points}, so shape/bulges survive a solve untouched. Circle and Round a corner (fillet) ship on this. Arc, Rectangle and Polygon are unblocked by it but wait on chrome2d below, which is a different blocker

build.name: Rectangle
build.why: CORRECTED: never representation-blocked. newSketch() already emits a rectangle (four points, typed in by hand), and a straight-edged polyline was always exactly the right shape for one -- the representation panel added nothing this needed. Blocked on chrome2d: there is no click-to-draw surface, only a 3D-projected drag overlay (HandleOverlay.tsx) over the preview iframe, and two clicks on empty sketch-plane space is not something that overlay can place yet

build.name: Arc
build.why: CORRECTED: representation-UNBLOCKED. bulges (see the shape item) expresses an arc exactly -- filletCorner() already builds one, tessellate() already samples one, HandleOverlay already draws one. What is missing is the same interaction surface rect and polygon are waiting on: a 3-Point or Tangent arc is drawn by clicking points on an empty sketch plane, and there is no click-to-draw surface yet, only a 3D-projected drag overlay with fixed handles at existing corners

build.name: Polygon
build.why: CORRECTED: never representation-blocked -- N points is exactly what a closed polyline already is, and generating them is a for-loop the student can see. Blocked on chrome2d, same as Rectangle: there is nowhere to click to place the shape before the loop can size it

build.name: Slice a corner
build.why: split out of the old 'fillet' item: Sketch Fillet shipped (Round a corner, via filletCorner() in lib/sketch-arc.ts -- rounds with an arc). A sketch-level CHAMFER slices the corner off flat instead: a straight replacement edge between two trim points, no bulge, no arc math. Same shape of work as the solid Angled Corner tool already does for a box or cylinder, not yet built for a sketch outline

build.name: Guide line
build.why: a line that positions other lines without becoming part of the outline -- the sketch equivalent of a variable

build.name: Trim
build.why: the tool that makes drawing forgiving; without it a wrong line must be undone rather than fixed

build.name: Mirror
build.why: symmetry and repetition inside the sketch, where they cost one line of code instead of a boolean

build.name: more rules
build.why: we have five of Onshape's sixteen. These five are the ones a beginner reaches for and the solver in lib/sketch-solve.ts can already express

build.name: the bar itself
build.why: CORRECTED: the bar already exists -- ModelEditor.tsx's .model-tools has grouped buttons, a FlyoutButton that collapses variants under a caret (the same drop-down pattern Onshape's own tools.htm describes), and a search box with matches() filtering, same as the feature toolbar. The Sketch group is the first group on it and now has three buttons (Sketch, Circle, Corner). What is genuinely missing: a click-to-draw SURFACE. The sketch editing surface is a 3D-projected drag overlay (HandleOverlay.tsx) over the preview iframe -- corners are dragged, not placed by clicking empty sketch-plane space -- so Rectangle, Arc and Polygon above are blocked here, on interaction, not on the representation panel this item used to gate them on

outOfScope.why: a spline's control points are a genuinely different mental model, and nothing in a first-year CS course needs a conic. The solver would also have to grow curvature continuity, which is a term no fourteen-year-old should meet in week three
each projects existing 3D geometry into the sketch plane, which needs addressable faces and edges. Same B-rep wall the feature toolbar hit
file import into a sandboxed iframe, plus a font pipeline for Text. The bundle does carry vectorText, so Text is the one here worth revisiting if a lesson wants a name plate
each is reachable once the representation lands, and none is needed before it. Queued behind the panel's decision rather than refused on principle -- revisit after the shape work

outOfScope.group: Variants of tools we build (4 tools)
outOfScope.why: a second way to draw a thing the student can already draw. Onshape offers them because a professional wants the fewest clicks for their particular case; a beginner offered two ways to draw a circle learns that there are two ways to draw a circle

outOfScope.group: Constraints the solver cannot express (3 tools)
outOfScope.why: concentric and tangent need arcs to exist first and then need the solver to handle curved-to-curved conditions, which lib/sketch-solve.ts does not do. Automatic inferencing is a whole guessing engine on top of that. Reconsider once arcs land

a point that is not a corner of the outline has nothing to reference it. In Onshape a sketch point is what a Hole feature snaps to; our Hole positions itself from its target's own centre instead, so a free point would be a dot the student can place and nothing can use. Revisit if Hole ever learns to snap.
